new_statements.rule_in_words: Cilambya (with Cisukwa and Cindali, 'SuNdaLa') is described as a two-tone (H/L) language: noun tone is lexical (H may sit on any mora), verb tone is culminative/'accentual' with exactly one H per verb whose position (penultimate vs antepenultimate mora or syllable) is fixed by tense-aspect morphology (imperative: penult mora, e.g. Cilambya ljaáŋga 'eat', lúma 'bite'; infinitive: antepenult mora). The thesis never posits or denies word stress for Cilambya.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said (only one H per verb; no tone spreading/doubling).
new_statements.exceptions: H placement in verbs varies by tense/aspect marker and allomorph (penult vs antepenult); monosyllabic roots take penult H in the infinitive; some infinitives with root-final sj/ʃ/z/lw/fj/vj show penult instead of antepenult H (p.135-136). These concern tone, not stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (citation/imperative forms and inflected verbs); pre-pausal penultimate vowel lengthening with falling tone is mentioned only second-hand for Cindali (p.27, reporting Mtenje A.D. 2006b), not stated for Cilambya. The only stress remark covering Lambya at all is Kashoki 1978's areal claim for Zambian languages (evenly stressed syllables, stress non-distinctive, p.70), which is not Lambya-specific.
new_statements.identity_note: Mtenje 2016 describes three Chitipa-district (northern Malawi) varieties jointly as 'SuNdaLa': Cisukwa (Glottolog sukw1242, a dialect of Ndali), Cindali (ndal1241) and Cilambya (lamb1272); the quoted generalisations are stated for all three and illustrated with separate Cilambya data (e.g. imperatives (62) p.129). Her Cilambya is the Malawian variety (T.A. Mwabulambya, Kameme etc.); Tanzanian (Ileje) and Zambian (Isoka) Lambya are not separately described. The same thesis already underlies the catalog entry for ndal1241 (classification tonal-OR-pitch accent). Kashoki 1978's stress remark is an areal statement about 'Zambian languages' (Zambian Lambya of Isoka is in his sample) and is not Lambya-specific.

sources.note: Ch.4 'Aspects of the Prosody of Cisukwa, Cindali and Cilambya' treats only tone and reduplication: two level tones H/L; noun tone lexical (H on any mora); verb tone 'accentual' with exactly one H per verb on the penultimate mora (imperatives, Cilambya ljaáŋga 'eat', lúma 'bite', p.129) or antepenultimate mora (infinitives), penult/antepenult syllable in other tenses (pp.127-146); contrastive vowel length (3.2.2 p.37); pre-pausal penultimate lengthening mentioned only when reporting Mtenje A.D. 2006b on Cindali (p.27). No sentence on word stress for Cilambya, neither asserting nor denying it.
